credentials.description: Bictorys public API key (Dashboard → Developers → API Keys → Public Key, prefix public-) sent as X-API-Key on this endpoint; sandbox and production keys differ

parameters.name: transactionId
parameters.description: UUID of the transaction to verify. Obtained from create_charge (transactionId or chargeId field) or from the webhook payload (id field).

example_prompt: Verify the status of a payment transaction to confirm it succeeded before fulfilling an order.

id.description: Transaction identifier. Observed null in the sandbox (2026-10-29, afrotools issue #175) on an unpaid hosted-checkout charge queried right after creation, with status "pending".

paymentMeans.description: Partially masked payment identifier, e.g. a masked phone number.

merchantFees.description: Fee amount charged to the merchant.

customerFees.description: Fee amount charged to the customer.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Defaults to XOF.

orderId.description: ID of the associated invoice, order, or payment link.

status.description: Transaction status. Bictorys' integration guide: "succeeded" → validate the order; "authorized" (card pre-capture) → treat as "succeeded"; "pending" / "processing" → wait, the webhook confirms the final status; "failed" / "cancelled" / "reversed" → mark failed. "authorized" means funds are reserved on the card, not yet captured — see gotchas and open_questions.

details.description: Bictorys error code. Examples: "E400-0: Bad transactionId is passed", "E404-1: Cannot find resource".

gotchas: Redirect query parameters are fully spoofable — never fulfill an order from them alone; call this endpoint server-side (or wait for the webhook) before trusting a redirect. A signature-verified webhook_payment_completed event, on the other hand, does not need this endpoint to be trusted — its HMAC/secret verification already proves authenticity, and gating fulfillment on a live call here risks losing an already-successful payment if this endpoint is briefly down (see the 500 gotcha below).

Use the PUBLIC key here (env BICTORYS_API_KEY, same key as create_charge, header X-API-Key). Bictorys' integration guide (docs.bictorys.com/docs/integration) lists "Status check (GET /pay/v1/transactions/{id}/status) | Clé publique (BICTORYS_API_KEY)" and "BICTORYS_API_KEY (publique) — Header X-Api-Key pour créer des charges et vérifier des transactions." The sandbox also accepts the PRIVATE key (BICTORYS_PRIVATE_KEY) on this endpoint — a live sandbox call measured 2026-09-14 (afrotools PR #67): both keys return 200 — so a sandbox-only test will not catch a wrong key. Do not rely on that permissiveness in production, and never send the private key from a frontend or mobile app.

Bictorys' integration guide ("Statuts possibles" table) says: `succeeded` — "Paiement confirmé" — "✅ Valider la commande"; `authorized` — "Paiement autorisé (pré-capture carte)" — "✅ Traiter comme `succeeded`"; `pending` and `processing` — "⏳ En attente — le webhook confirmera le statut final"; `failed`, `cancelled`, `reversed` — "❌ Marquer FAILED". "authorized" means funds are reserved but not yet captured: the API reference describes create_charge's `authorization: true` as a request to "reserve an amount on the holder card to pay later the transaction", and has a separate endpoint to "capture totally or partially a transaction previously authorized" (the capture_charge spec: POST /pay/v1/captures?transactionId=…). Whether fulfilling on "authorized" without a capture is safe is not stated — see open_questions.
The transactionId to pass here is the id field from the webhook payload, or the transactionId / chargeId field from the create_charge response — they refer to the same transaction UUID.

id can be null: on 2026-10-29, in the sandbox, a status check on an unpaid hosted-checkout charge (create_charge HTTP 202, chargeId), made right after creation, returned HTTP 200 {"id":null,"status":"pending"} (integration report, afrotools issue #175). Do not take the transaction id from this response: use the id you put in the path.

Sandbox, to reach succeeded: Bictorys documents test cards (docs.bictorys.com/docs/cartes-bancaires-de-test): enter a first and last name of your choice, a future expiry date and a CVV; 2303779999000275 (frictionless) and 2303779999000408 (challenge, the OTP to enter on the challenge page is 1234) succeed; 2303779999000291, 2303779999000317, 2303779999000424 and 2303779999000432 fail (not authenticated, or unavailable). Mobile money in the sandbox runs on a simulator (docs.bictorys.com/docs/test-mobile-money): a QR code is shown, to scan with the phone's camera only, never with a real Wave, Orange Money or MTN app. In the sandbox, the success and error redirect URLs are not called after a mobile money payment: test a redirect with a card.

A transactionId taken from the redirect comes from the browser: prefer the one you stored, since unencoded, a visitor's "../…" would send this call, with your private key, to another endpoint. The docs type it as a uuid — create_charge: "transactionId": { "description": "Unique Id of the initiated transaction", "type": "string", "format": "uuid" }. The example passes it through encodeURIComponent: an empty value, "." or ".." still changes the path, and the value must be the decoded one (URLSearchParams.get decodes it), or it is encoded twice.
Sandbox base URL is https://api.test.bictorys.com — the production URL is https://api.bictorys.com.

On status 'succeeded', this endpoint returns NO amount and NO timestamp — observed live: {"id": "…", "status": "succeeded"} and nothing else. Reading status and amount from the same response therefore yields 0 for the amount ON THE SUCCESS PATH, which in a billing system means crediting nothing while everything reports success. Fall back to GET /pay/v1/transactions and match on paymentReference to obtain amount and timestamp.

The list endpoint GET /pay/v1/transactions (undocumented) only becomes non-empty once a transaction COMPLETES. It stays [] while a charge is merely pending, which makes reference-based lookup look untestable in sandbox until the first successful payment.
In the Bictorys sandbox, GET /pay/v1/transactions/{id}/status is known to return HTTP 500 intermittently. For sandbox testing, rely on webhook events instead of polling this endpoint.

Bictorys recommends polling this endpoint for backend-less apps (e.g. static/mobile-only clients that can't expose a webhook endpoint). Apps with a backend server should treat webhook_payment_completed as the source of truth for fulfillment, and use this endpoint for the redirect-triggered UX check and for reconciliation (e.g. a periodic sweep of orders whose webhook never arrived) — not as a mandatory gate after every webhook.
open_questions: Bictorys' integration guide says to treat "authorized" ("Paiement autorisé (pré-capture carte)") as "succeeded", while the API reference describes an authorization as an amount reserved on the card "to pay later the transaction" and offers a capture endpoint ("Capture totally or partially a transaction previously authorized"). Does "authorized" only occur for card charges created with authorization: true, and must the merchant capture before the funds are collected — i.e. is fulfilling an order on "authorized" safe without a capture?

Is id null only before the customer chooses a payment method on the hosted checkout (HTTP 202 flow), or also for a pending direct-flow charge (HTTP 201), for processing, and in production? Only a sandbox, hosted-checkout, pending case has been observed (afrotools issue #175).
